mbm-2876.clue: The radio crackles in the rhythm of the rain.
mbm-2876.quote: On a wet night a ham friend described sunshine falling on his kitchen floor. I drew the square of yellow by my log and posted it to him later. His sun came back with our rain painted over it.

mbm-2877.clue: My best save lives on a piece of cardboard.
mbm-2877.quote: Our adventure game forgot its save after a power cut. My sister had drawn our map on a cereal box. We followed the little blue hills right back to the place we'd lost.

mbm-2878.clue: The yellow disc has a bite on the rim.
mbm-2878.quote: My nephew cut a crescent of yellow paper to look like our old frisbee with a dog bite. He stands beside me throwing his own disc at my shadow. Some of his throws catch me by surprise.

mbm-2879.clue: I learned how loud a zipper can be.
mbm-2879.quote: I recorded my first parachute landing from a camera on the ground. The loudest sound on the whole tape is my dad unzipping the bag to find his glasses. He made it in time to see me wave.

mbm-2880.clue: Our tallest pawn is a pine cone.
mbm-2880.quote: We play park chess beside a pine tree. When a pawn reaches the last rank we give it a little cone crown. A windy afternoon can turn the ending into a very mixed forest.

mbm-2881.clue: My poles know when lunchtime is due.
mbm-2881.quote: I wrapped one pole grip in blue tape for breaking left and the other in red for right. Between them is my brother's drawing of our thermos and my plaid cup with the steam curling up. That's my favorite run on the map.

mbm-2882.clue: My oldest quilt has one bare branch.
mbm-2882.quote: I left one of the tree branches plain for the family member who hadn't arrived yet. My niece was born in autumn. She chose a leaf the color of a plum for it when she turned four.

mbm-2883.clue: I keep a red pea in the sugar bowl.
mbm-2883.quote: I painted one wooden pea bright red for my cup trick so the back row would see it. After the show Mum puts it in the sugar bowl so I don't lose it. Nobody has mistaken it for sugar yet.

mbm-2884.clue: We draw the curl with a wet thumb.
mbm-2884.quote: After curling I trace our favorite shot on the steamy warming-room window. By the time the tea is cool the line has vanished. My skip draws it again, only a little closer to the button.

mbm-2885.clue: My hero got a haircut in the margin.
mbm-2885.quote: I write my first drafts on envelopes. During one long scene my niece drew the hero a crooked fringe in the corner. I couldn't stop picturing it and sent him to the barber in chapter five.

mbm-2886.clue: The antenna shares the roof with a sparrow.
mbm-2886.quote: A sparrow sat on my antenna all morning while I spoke to a station overseas. I drew it on my confirmation card and wrote that we had two operators at this end.

mbm-2887.clue: The ribbon knows the shortcut home.
mbm-2887.quote: I do a trick with two rings and a blue ribbon. My mother taught me to tie the neat little bow at the finish. The rings amaze the children. The bow always gets a nod from Mum.

mbm-2888.clue: I built a robot whose knee actually squeaks.
mbm-2888.quote: My model's knee hinge protested the first time I posed it. I kept the squeak and made it a mechanic leaning on a cane. My workshop finally has somebody qualified to complain about the stairs.

mbm-2889.clue: I have to fold the night shift inward.
mbm-2889.quote: My sister works nights and slept through our quilting bee on the couch. We pieced little dark-blue eyelids into the blanket we made for her. Fold it over at the top and they close. She tried it out before we even put the kettle on.

mbm-2890.clue: I gave the rabbit one bent ear.
mbm-2890.quote: When I cut rows of paper rabbits for our window, one ear folded on itself. I made its shadow long and left the ear just so. That rabbit looks as though it knows the best secret.

mbm-2891.clue: My ball leaves a moon on the towel.
mbm-2891.quote: When I wipe my bowling ball after a good frame, the oil leaves a pale curve on my dark towel. I don't wash it till league night is over. My score takes care of the rest of the phases.

mbm-2892.clue: I had to take my prize home sideways.
mbm-2892.quote: Our town fair gave the winner of the corn contest a gigantic straw hat. It wouldn't fit through the bus door flat. Half the passengers leaned over to help, and everybody wanted to try it on.

mbm-2893.clue: We play the longest hole in three photos.
mbm-2893.quote: My son takes one picture from the tee, one from where my ball lands and one from the green. From those three frames my father can tell whether I took the shortcut through the trees again.

mbm-2894.clue: My chalk bag belonged to a shopkeeper.
mbm-2894.quote: I took the pocket from my granddad's old hardware-shop apron and stitched it into a bag for climbing chalk. There was still one square-headed nail in the seam. I keep that on the shelf at home.

mbm-2895.clue: A detective has to share the blanket.
mbm-2895.quote: At pajama mystery night we put a cushion in the empty seat for the detective. If the ending is clever we lend the cushion a corner of our blanket. One winter the cushion was very well looked after.

mbm-2896.clue: I learned to quilt on a round table.
mbm-2896.quote: When hard times made our quilting bee give up its hall, the cafe down the street gave us a round table for Sunday mornings. We made the owner a round quilted table mat with a wedge for every regular. Mine has one real tea stain. I had to work on it somewhere.

mbm-2897.clue: My nails can put the kettle on.
mbm-2897.quote: I painted a blue teapot on one thumbnail and a cup on the other. When I tilt them together my little cousin holds out the tiniest biscuit she can find. Tea parties travel lightly round here.

mbm-2898.clue: The trail has a tiny place for a whistle.
mbm-2898.quote: Halfway along our walk there's a crack in the stone wall that catches the wind. I sit by it to eat lunch. A quiet day means I have to whistle our usual tune myself.

mbm-2899.clue: My model built the stage for its own photograph.
mbm-2899.quote: I wanted a proper launch platform for my mecha model, so I stacked the sprues the parts came on into a little scaffold. All those empty outlines look like windows. I lit it from underneath and the robot stole its own opening night.

mbm-2900.clue: Our ending credits wear a different scarf every week.
mbm-2900.quote: We ran an anime screening in a draughty room and took turns bringing the scarf that kept the door from rattling. At the end of the season we drew the whole club, including the door wearing all eight scarves. I got the Saturday stripes right from memory.
